claims.text: The alloy's anomalous thermoelastic and stress–strain responses are governed by residual stresses induced by local thermal-expansion mismatches.
HfNbTaTiZr has an inherently heterogeneous microstructure.
Conventional casting and cold rolling produce compositional and microstructural heterogeneity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The heterogeneous regions have localized differences in thermal-expansion coefficients.
Local thermal-expansion differences generate internal residual stresses during cooling from processing temperatures.
The cooling-induced residual stresses alter dislocation dynamics.
The cooling-induced residual stresses alter the activation energy of deformation processes.
Residual stresses influence the high-temperature creep rate of HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual stresses influence the temperature dependence of the alloy's elastic modulus.
Residual stresses influence aging-induced hardening in the alloy.
Extended homogenization will reduce local compositional inhomogeneity.
Extended homogenization will improve the uniformity of lattice parameters.
Reduced compositional inhomogeneity and more uniform lattice parameters will minimize local thermal-expansion mismatch.
Homogenized samples will have lower residual stresses than standard cast and cold-rolled samples after controlled cooling.
Homogenized samples will exhibit a lower tensile creep rate at 1250 °C than standard processed samples.
Homogenized samples will exhibit a smaller change in elastic modulus between 293 and 1100 K than standard processed samples.
Homogenized samples will exhibit less aging-induced hardening at 600–800 °C than standard processed samples.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify creep testing only at 1250 °C, whereas the boundary describes a room-temperature-to-1250 °C range for creep. It is unclear whether creep is to be measured only at 1250 °C or across that full range.
